subject: Reasoning
description: Classic two-statement DS format — common in banking PO papers

questions.stem: Question: What is the age of Raj? Statement I: Raj is 5 years older than Mohan. Statement II: Mohan is 20 years old.

options.option_text: Both statements together are sufficient but neither alone

questions.explanation: Statement I alone: Raj = Mohan + 5 — we don't know Mohan. Not sufficient. Statement II alone: gives only Mohan. Not sufficient. Together: Raj = 20 + 5 = 25. Sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Question: Is x a positive number? Statement I: x + 3 > 0. Statement II: x² > 9.
questions.explanation: I alone: x > −3 — could be 0 or negative (e.g. −2), not only positive. Not sufficient. II alone: |x| > 3 — could be x > 3 OR x < −3, not only positive. Not sufficient. Together: x > −3 AND |x| > 3 → x > 3 → positive. Sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Question: In which DIRECTION is point A from point B? Statement I: A is east of C. Statement II: C is north of B.
questions.explanation: Need to locate A relative to B. I alone: A is east of C but C's position vs B unknown. Not sufficient. II alone: C north of B, A unplaced. Not sufficient. Together: B→north to C→east to A ⇒ A is north-east of B. Sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Question: How many sons does Mr. X have? Statement I: Mr. X has 4 children. Statement II: He has 2 daughters.
questions.explanation: I alone: 4 children — but sons/daughters split unknown. II alone: 2 daughters — but total unknown. Together: 4 − 2 = 2 sons. Sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Question: What is Hindi-score of Prakash? Statement I: Prakash's average score across 3 subjects is 60. Statement II: Prakash scored 55 in English and 65 in Maths.
questions.explanation: I alone: average = 60, so sum = 180, but individual Hindi unknown. II alone: English + Maths = 120, Hindi unknown. Together: Hindi = 180 − 120 = 60. Sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Question: What is the value of x? Statement I: 2x + 5 = 15. Statement II: x² − 25 = 0.
questions.explanation: I alone: 2x = 10 → x = 5. Unique solution. Sufficient. II alone: x = ±5 — not unique. Not sufficient. So Statement I ALONE is sufficient.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Question: What is the SMALLER of two integers whose sum is 25? Statement I: One integer is 11 more than the other. Statement II: The integers are both positive.
questions.explanation: I alone: a + b = 25 and difference = 11 → larger = 18, smaller = 7. Sufficient. II alone: just tells us both are positive — infinitely many pairs. Not sufficient. I ALONE suffices.
